31
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, August 8, 2011/Sravana 17, 1933 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Coal; Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Corporate
Affairs; Earth Sciences; Information and Broadcasting; Law and Justice;
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises; Mines; Minority Affairs;
New and Renewable Energy; Parliamentary Affairs; Power;
Science and Technology; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Disturbance in frequencies of
channels
†*101. SHRI ISHWARLAL
SHANKARLAL JAIN: Will the Minister
of INFORMA TION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether there are frequent changes
in the frequencies of channels being shown
through Direct-to-Home (DTH) by satellite
of Doordarshan;
(b) whether Government proposes to
bring more channels within the ambit of
DTH;
(c) whether Marathi IBN-Lokmat
channel which was earlier being shown
through DTH, is no longer available on
DTH for many months; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
Scheme for minority dominated
districts of Madhya Pradesh
†*102. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the
Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a proposal
of Madhya Pradesh Government pertaining
to development scheme for minority
dominated districts is pending with the
Ministry;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Ministry has taken any
decision thereon; and
(d) if not, by when a decision would be
taken?
Achievement of RGGVY target
*103. SHRI KANWAR DEEP SINGH:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the targets fixed for
electrification of villages during each of the
last three years under the Rajiv Gandhi
Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana (RGGVY)
have been achieved in various States
including Jharkhand;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

32
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Allocation of coal blocks to private
companies
*104. SHRI PRAKASH JAV ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) how many coal blocks were allocated
to private companies during the period 2006
to 2009;
(b) the details of such coal blocks,
including coal reserves, allocated to private
companies;
(c) the reasons for such allocations and
since when the Bill to auction coal blocks
is pending in the Parliament;
(d) whether all these companies have
established production units in steel/
cement/power sectors; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Progress of Panchnad dam
†*105. SHRI GANGA CHARAN : Will
the Minister of WA TER RESOURCES  be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the progress made with
regard to the  project of Panchnad dam
proposed by the State Governments of
Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh;
(b) whether this project can be included
in the special package given to the
Bundelkhand region; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Corruption in CIL
*106. SHRI DHIRAJ PRASAD SAHU:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has received
any complaints of alleged corruption
prevailing in the Coal India Ltd. (CIL);
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the number of complaints received during
the last three years and the current year,
subsidiary-wise and year-wise;
(c) whether Government has conducted
any investigation into these complaints;
(d) if so, the outcome thereof,
subsidiary-wise;
(e) the details of the officers against
whom charges were framed by the
investigating agencies and those punished
or exonerated as a result thereof,
subsidiary-wise; and
(f) the effective measures taken by
Government in this regard?
Joint Group of Experts on Flood
Management
*107. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the Minister of W A TER RESOURCES
be pleased to refer to the answer to Starred
Question 371 given in the Rajya Sabha on
19 August, 2010 and state:
(a) the details of the follow-up action
taken after the meeting of the Joint Group
of Experts on Flood Management between
Government of India and the Royal
Government of Bhutan; and
(b) the details of the steps taken to save
the people of North Bengal who are affected
by floods every year?
Availability of channels on DTH
†*108. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD: Will the Minister of
INFORMATION AND
BROADCASTING be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that under the
prevailing circumstances, a common
television viewer has been left at the mercy
of Direct-to-Home (DTH) operators;

33
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if not, Government's reaction
thereto;
(c) whether it is also a fact that a
common viewer is forced to watch such
channels for which he does not pay;
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(e) whether, while implementing the
existing system, Government had assured
that the common viewer would watch only
those channels which he would opt for?
Construction of community study
centres
*109. DR. BHALCHANDRA
MUNGEKAR: Will the Minister of
MINORITY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Sachar Committee had
raised concerns over the fact that a
substantial proportion of households in
urban settlements live in one room
accommodation and it is absolutely
necessary to create local community study
centres for students so that they can spend
a few hours to concentrate on their studies;
(b) whether there is any Government
scheme to construct community study
centres in urban slums; and
(c) whether the Member of Parliament
Local Area Development Scheme
(MPLADS)  funds could be utilized for
this purpose?
Electoral reforms
*110. SHRI RAMDAS AGARW AL:
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Chief Election
Commissioner has recommended for early
electoral reforms as there is large scale
corruption in the existing electoral system
and the role of criminals and money power
is rampant;
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
to ensure that the law breakers are not
allowed to become law makers;
(c) whether any draft legislation in this
regard is being brought before the
Parliament during the Monsoon Session;
and
(d) whether Government is also in
favour of making compulsory maintenance
of accounts by the political parties and the
audit thereof by the agencies specified by
the Comptroller and Auditor General of
India?
Unelectrified villages and households
†*111. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that around 1.25
lakh villages in the country are yet to be
electrified and around 8 crore households
have no access to power;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) if not, the status thereof?
Cases pending with the Maulana Azad
Education Foundation
*112. SHRI SABIR ALI: Will the
Minister of MINORITY AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of various cases pending
with the Maulana Azad Education
Foundation;
(b) since when each of these cases is
pending; and
(c) the reasons for the pendency and
the action being taken to clear them
expeditiously?

34
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Damage to foodgrains and food items
due to rains
†*113. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of
large scale damage to foodgrains and food
items, caused by rains in many States due
to lack of proper storage facilities;
(b) the details thereof indicating the
quantum of such losses during the last year,
State-wise; and
(c) the details of the measures taken by
Government to stop such losses?
National Water Policy
*114. SHRI ISHWAR SINGH: Will the
Minister of W ATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has assessed
the demand of water in the country during
the next one decade or so;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government proposes to
formulate a National Water Policy, in view
of the increasing demand of water; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Procurement of wheat
†*115. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there was a
direction from Government to procure
wheat upto 31 May, 2011;
(b) whether wheat was procured even
on 1 June, 2011, against the direction, in
Sehore, Jabalpur and some other districts
of Madhya Pradesh;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
procurement of wheat at many places was
made from middlemen instead of farmers,
as a result of which loan register numbers
and sown areas were not mentioned against
the name of farmers;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the action taken by Government in
this matter?
Convertibility of set-top box
†*116. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to
technical and economic reasons, set-top box
being non convertible, common viewer has
become helpless before Direct-to-Home
(DTH) operators;
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(c) whether Government would
consider to protect the common viewer by
making new arrangements?
Wind energy potential in Kerala
*117. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of NEW AND RENEWABLE
ENERGY be pleased to state:
(a) the estimated potential of wind
energy in Kerala;
(b) the quantum of wind energy tapped
till now in the State;

35
(c) whether the State Government has
submitted any proposal for setting up of
new wind energy projects in the State; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken thereon?
Meeting of Revisionary Authorities
*118. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of MINES be pleased to
refer to the answer to Starred Question 258
given in the Rajya Sabha on 14 March, 2011
and state:
(a) how often the Revisionary
Authorities for different States meet
annually;
(b) when the last such meeting of the
respective Revisionary Authorities for the
States of Chhattisgarh and Karnataka took
place;
(c) whether Government would ensure
that small entrepreneurs get a proper hearing
at such meetings;
(d) whether it is mandatory that an
aggrieved person must be represented by
advocates; and
(e) if so, the steps taken to simplify the
system for small entrepreneurs and
aggrieved persons?
Swaminathan Commission on storage
requirement
*119. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the details of additional storage/
warehouse facilities needed for storage of
foodgrains;
(b) whether the Swaminathan
Commission had made any suggestions
regarding storage requirement;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) whether Government is going to
implement those recommendations?
Export of foodgrains
*120. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has recently
decided to export foodgrains instead of
distributing the excess stock among the
poor;
(b) if so, under what pressing
circumstances Government has taken this
step;
(c) whether Government has allowed
traders to export foodgrains; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 2nd August, 2011 Secretary-General.
Sravana 11, 1933 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Coal : 104, 106,
Consumer Affairs, Food and :
Public Distribution 113, 115, 119, 120,
Corporate Affairs :—
Earth Sciences :—
Information and Broadcasting : 101, 108, 116,
Law and Justice : 110,
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises :—
Mines : 118,
Minority Affairs : 102, 109, 112,
New and Renewable Energy : 117,
Parliamentary Affairs :—
Power : 103, 111,
Science and Technology :—
Water Resources : 105, 107, 114.
36
